intro1:
A kaleidoscope has infinite colours: reds. blues. yellows. greens.
Warm. Garish. Toxic. Soothing. Sometimes the colours blend. Much like how people treat one another.
There is love, kindness, understanding, courtesy, compassion. Or also: rudeness, lies, hatred, polemics, persecution, violence.
intro2: Together with pupils from the Europa-Gymnasium Frankfurt (Oder), the music school and the Singakademie Frankfurt (Oder), as well as the lyceum at the Collegium Polonicum in Słubice, we want to explore and discuss these themes on the basis of the historical story of Jesus of Nazareth – with the help of music by Johann Sebastian Bach from his two famous passions: the St Matthew and St John Passions. Alongside these come pieces by the Argentine inventor of tango nuevo, Astor Piazzolla – for example from his opera »Maria de Buenos Aires«. Musical direction is by our new principal conductor, Felix Mildenberger.
intro3: Are the colours between people always clear-cut? Do they blend? What comes of it? How does it affect us? How can we live well together?
intro4: We want to explore all these questions artistically together with the German and Polish pupils: through choreography, film, singing, acting and drawing.
closing: What will come of it? Colourful, we hope. Just like a kaleidoscope. And perhaps – some insight, too.

termin2: Mon · 12 Oct 2026 · 12:00 pm — Collegium Polonicum, Słubice
musik_intro: Johann Sebastian Bach and Astor Piazzolla. Why did we choose music by these two seemingly so opposite composers, from completely different eras and cultures? Why do we believe their music expresses especially well what we want to say to young people? Perhaps because their music is almost visually predestined to express the themes we have chosen. Perhaps because Piazzolla, from an early age, was fascinated not only by tango, but even earlier by the great baroque composer Bach.
musik_intro2: Or perhaps quite simply because a sentence by Martin Luther applies to their music:
luther_zitat: “Music is a pure gift and a gift of God, it drives away the devil, it makes people cheerful, and one forgets all vices through it.”
mitmachen: As a member of the Förderverein, you help make projects like Kaleidoskop possible – and enable children and young people from Frankfurt (Oder) and Słubice to bring music, theatre and big questions to the stage together.
